support_text: The study investigated chronic effects induced in vitro by benzo[a]pyrene (B[a]P) prolonged exposure on gilthead sea bream (Sparus aurata L.) hepatocytes, evaluating cellular and nuclear latent damage. Short-term effects at higher B[a]P doses were linked to higher cytotoxicities and necrotic lysis, whereas a sustained inflammatory response at medium-low doses was perceived as a mitochondria-mediated apoptosis, both by surface and nuclear morphological changes. The strong immunoreactivity for cleaved caspase-3 showed that labeled cells committed suicide by apoptosis.
